brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.evidence: No holder built. 3D-printed plastic softens near a switched-on hot iron; the configurator checks fit only and knows nothing about heat resistance. Use a metal/coiled stand for the hot iron.
requirements.requirement: holder for the iron while switched on and hot

requirements.evidence: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-half with solder-reel prop; bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-half-div2 with tips stand-in prop
requirements.requirement: two bins for solder and spare tips

finish.summary: Built a 2-cell joined base with two half-depth bins: one for solder, one divided for spare tips (staged with props). No hot-iron holder: unsafe in printed plastic, so use a metal stand for the hot iron.

lines.key: pvc-section-double  (cut 18 mm from 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US))
lines.label: pvc-section-double (cut 18 mm from 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US))

cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes

events.text: Your hot iron needs metal, not plastic — I'll build the cold-parts storage I safely can.
